_readme: Every knob of the Tiers page (tiers.html), in one place. The pipeline
copies this file into assets/data/sheet_tiers.v1.js; the page does the
maths in the browser (assets/js/app/tierstats.js) so the as-of date and
the date range can move freely. Edit, then run
`python3 pipeline/sheet_sync.py rebuild`.
WIN VALUE. A map result is worth more when it is harder or bigger:
importance = event weight x bracket weight
value      = importance x (result - expected), where `expected` is the
winner's chance from the two teams' POWER ratings at the
time the map was played. Beating a stronger team is worth
a lot; beating a much weaker one is worth little; losing
to a weaker one costs a lot.
POWER RATING (per team, as of any date) = Elo + standings:
* Elo starts at the team's region tier (`regionTier`) and moves after
every map, by `elo.k` x importance x (result - expected). So
international LANs and playoff maps move ratings the most, and
international results are what settle cross-region strength.
* standings: the team's map-win share in its CURRENT regional stage,
shrunk toward 50% by `standings.priorMaps` (half won, half lost),
adds blend x points x 2 x (share - 50%) rating points: a perfect
record is worth +blend x points, a winless one -blend x points.
HERO SCORE per map and role (tiers are cut within each role):
pick share    = order-weighted listings / team-maps (see listWeights)
adjusted win  = 50% + sum(share x value) / (sum(share x importance) + shrink)
score         = 100 x (pick.weight x sqrt(pick share / best pick share in role)
+ win.weight  x (clamp((adjusted win - 50%) / win.span, -1, 1) + 1) / 2)
(the square root keeps the second- and third-most-picked heroes
of a role close to the first instead of halving them)
tier          = first band whose `min` the score reaches; heroes under
`minPicks` order-weighted listings, or under `minPickShare` of
the team-maps in view, are listed as 'low sample'. Comps need
`compMinMaps` maps and are tiered across all comps on the map.

tiers.blurb: Defines the meta here: the heroes most teams build around, or popular picks that win above what the matchups predict.
Strong, regular picks, or less common ones that beat good opposition.
Solid options: either popular with average results or niche with good ones.
Situational: seen now and then, results are mixed.
Rarely picked here, or losing more than expected when it is.
